newsitem.title: USA: Portland Natural estimates joint system costs.
newsitem.headline: Portland Natural estimates joint system costs.

text.p: Portland Natural Gas Transmission System said its proposed joint venture with the Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline would add nearly $60 million to the cost of its system to deliver natural gas from the TransCanada PipeLines Ltd system near Vermont's Canadian border to Massachusetts.

Portland Natural's PNGTS Operating Co LLC unit said its proposal to build 48 miles of laterals to serve newly signed customers would raise the cost of its proposal to $303 million from the $271 million previously projected while cutting its 242 mile length by nearly 18 miles.

Increasing the capacity of 224 miles from the Canadian border to Haverhill, Maine, enough to also handle Maritimes proposed Sable Island volumes would increase the cost to $361 million, PNGTS estimated.
Over this segment, the two systems had proposed nearly parallel routes. This resulted in U.S. regulators instructing the two systems to discuss a joint system.

Maritimes spokesman Jim Grasso said the system has not yet filed its proposal for joint operations in this area, but did release the latest report to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on the status of talks between the two systems.

It said they met October 23 in Boston to discuss substantive and timing issues with respect to a possible joint pipeline. At that time two task forces were established to discuss routes and permitting.
They met on October 29 and 31, respectively, and the permit task force is scheduled to meet again on November 12.

Besides TransCanada, owners of the Portland Natural Gas system include Bay State Gas Co, Tenneco Inc, Gaz Metropolitain and Co LP, MCN Corp and U.S. Generating, owned by Pacific Gas and Electric Co and Bechtel Group Inc.
The first phase of the Maritime system was proposed by PanEnergy Corp, Westcoast Energy Inc, Eastern Enterprises and Mobil Corp.
